newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Volkswagen hit by second S.Africa strike.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen hit by second S.Africa strike.

text.p: German automaker Volkswagen's plant in South Africa's Eastern Cape stood shut for a fourth day on Friday following another wave of protests by about 4,000 employees since Tuesday, a spokesman said.

Volkswagen's spokesman Raymond Hartle said the Uitenhage assembly plant, which had only resumed normal production last week after a three day strike over the company's cost-cutting measures, had again been officially closed on Thursday.

He said the employees, belonging to the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (NUMSA), had downed tools on Tuesday to protest the company's move to discipline two of their colleagues in connection with the past strike which started on March 18.

Hartle said the two employees had been suspended with full pay over allegations that one assaulted a fellow worker during the last strike, while the other was alleged to have damaged Volkswagen's property.
"The company officially closed the plant yesterday (Thursday) and there will also be no production today (Friday)," he told Reuters.

"The union is currently consulting its members who are not happy with the disciplinary action the company has taken against the two workers. We don't know if production will resume again on Monday," Hartle said, adding there were talks between NUMSA and management scheduled for later on Friday to try seek a resolution of the situation.
The Uitenhage plant produces around 320 vehicles a day valued at about 16 million rand, the company said.
NUMSA officials could not be reached for comment.
